title: Asteroid Collision
hints: a collision only happens between a right-mover and a later left-mover, and the outcome of one collision can trigger another with whatever survived just before it - which structure lets you 'undo' the most recent survivor easily?
walk through asteroids left to right, keeping a stack of surviving asteroids so far. push right-movers directly, they can't collide yet
when a left-mover arrives, it may need to fight the top of the stack repeatedly: while the stack top is a smaller positive asteroid, pop it (it explodes) and keep checking the new top

after that loop, if the stack top is now a positive asteroid of equal size, pop it and discard the left-mover too (both explode); if the top is positive and still bigger, discard the left-mover; if the stack is empty or the top is also negative, push the left-mover
commonMistakes: only checking the immediate previous asteroid once instead of looping while the current asteroid keeps winning against the stack top
mishandling the equal-size case (forgetting both should be destroyed, not just one)
treating a negative asteroid meeting another negative asteroid (or positive meeting positive) as a collision when same-direction asteroids never collide

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of integers representing asteroids in a row, all moving at the same speed. Each asteroid's absolute value is its size, and its sign is its direction: positive means moving right, negative means moving left.

**Return the state of the asteroids after all collisions have been resolved, from left to right.**

When two moving asteroids meet, the smaller one explodes; if they're the same size, both explode. Two asteroids moving in the same direction never collide.
notes: all asteroids moving the same direction (no collisions at all)
a chain of collisions where one surviving asteroid then collides again with the next one
equal-size collision where both asteroids are destroyed

sampleTestCases.explanation: 10 (moving right) collides with -5 (moving left); 10 is bigger, so -5 explodes and 10 survives; 5 was already moving right and never meets anything
equal sizes moving toward each other - both explode
2 (moving right) collides with -5 (moving left) first; 2 is smaller so it explodes; then -5 collides with 10; -5 is smaller so it explodes; 10 survives untouched

optimal.pattern: stack (only the most recently surviving asteroid can collide with the next one)

bruteForce.approach: repeatedly scan the array for any adjacent right-moving-then-left-moving pair and resolve that one collision, rebuilding the array, until no more collisions are found
